entries.text: Train body. This is the body of the train. Its smooth nose helps air flow around it.
Driver’s cab. The driver sits here. The controls help the driver run the train.
Passenger windows. We can look outside through these windows. What can you see on a train ride?
Roof. The roof covers the carriage. It helps keep the rain outside.
Seats. Passengers sit on these seats. There is a path between the rows.
Doors. We use the doors to get on and off. Wait until the train stops and the doors open.
Bogies. These frames hold the wheels under the train. They support the carriage and help it follow curves.
Traction motors. These motors use electricity. They turn the wheels through gears to move the train.
Pantograph. This arm reaches up from the roof. It takes electric power from a wire above the train.
Coupler. This part joins one carriage to another. It helps keep the train connected.
Driver’s seat. The driver sits here and watches the track ahead.
Driver’s desk. The driver controls the train from this desk.
Displays. These screens show the speed and the signals.
Body shell. The body is a strong tube that carries the load.
Cabin floor. The floor carries the seats and hides the equipment.
Luggage rack. Bags ride above the seats.
Air-conditioning unit. The air-conditioning unit sits on the roof.
Supply duct. Treated air travels through these ducts.
Window glazing. The glass lets light in and keeps noise out.
Window blind. This blind rolls down to block the sun.
Seat cushion. The cushion is soft, and a frame holds it up.
Seat back. The seat back supports your back.
Door leaf and seal. This door slides along the side of the train to open.
Door sensor and light. Sensors watch the doorway before the doors close.
Bogie frame. This H-shaped frame carries the wheels.
Wheelset. One axle joins two wheels into a wheelset.
Air spring. Air springs make the ride smooth.
Traction motor. These motors turn electricity into motion.
Gearbox. The gearbox slows the motor but adds force.
Cooling duct. Air flows through here to cool the motors.
Insulator. These parts hold the live arm above the roof.
Folding arm. The arms fold and unfold to reach the wire.
Collector head. The collector head slides along the wire.
Coupler head. The coupler head locks onto the next carriage.
Energy absorber. This absorbs the push between carriages.
